TASK: Brain oscillations (alpha/beta/gamma/theta) in the mesh, as measurable opt-in wrappers around the existing Router (wrap warm-started robust Hebbian: see shortlab.rs for how it's built) and benchmarked in sim.rs Scenario variants and drift/failure windows. Hypotheses:
(a) ALPHA = periodic inhibition of exploration: oscillating temperature/epsilon schedule (e.g. period P tasks, duty cycle) vs constant temp; sweep P and amplitude on seeds 1-8.
(b) GAMMA synchrony: only agents whose recent-success phase is coherent (e.g. EMA of success above threshold, tracked on a gamma cycle) are recruited; weight consolidation (apply batched Hebbian update) every G tasks vs online.
(c) THETA-GAMMA coupling: working-memory slots, k items per theta cycle, replay recent outcomes (task,agent,reward) into the router at theta boundaries; test replay on/off, k in {2,4,8}.
(d) BETA status-quo: stickiness bonus to the currently routed agent per task type until a surprise burst (reward prediction error beyond threshold) releases it.
Plus a combined stack only if singles show promise. Each wrapper implements the Router trait. Include controls: a constant-phase (non-oscillating) variant with same average temp, and a phase-randomized oscillation, to show any gain is from the oscillation structure and not just a retuned temperature. Evaluate on all available Scenario variants plus failure/drift windows. Write results/r1_oscillations.json. Report honestly if nothing beats warm(hebbian-robust).

handback.t:
R1 report: brain-oscillation wrappers (alpha, gamma, theta-gamma, beta) do NOT beat warm(hebbian-robust). 0 Holm-significant wins in any world.

**Files**
- `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\oscillations.rs`: `OscRouter` wraps `Warm<HebbianRouter>` and implements `Router`. With all mechanisms off it is identical to plain `Warm` (tested). Configs are serde-default, nothing existing was edited, and it has 9 unit tests that pass. One line was appended to `src/lib.rs`: `pub mod oscillations;`.
- `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\bin\r1_oscillations.rs`
- `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\r1_oscillations.json`
- Board entry appended to `results/research_board.md` under "R1 oscillations".

**Rerun** (about 13 s; use `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r1` and the usual PATH): `cargo run --release --bin r1_oscillations`. Unit tests: `cargo test --release --lib oscillations`.

**Protocol**
- Tuned on seeds 1-8, evaluated on held-out seeds 31-60 with paired 95% t-CI.
- Worlds: the four sim.rs Scenarios (fixed, random, no-synergy, no-traps; all have drift and a failure window) plus a stationary shortlab-style control world with no drift or failures.
- Windows: all, pre-drift, failure, early-post-drift, late-post-drift.
- Holm over 154 candidate cells, each against the best fair baseline for that world and window.
- Baselines were tuned: eps-greedy, pooled-ts, hebbian-robust, and warm with k=30 and Global evidence.
- random and no-synergy are identical for solo routing, so there are really 4 distinct sim worlds plus the control.

**Tuning-seed results** (objective, warm = 0.7774): alpha-square 0.7742, gate 0.7780, batch 0.7766, theta k=2/4/8 0.7781/0.7751/0.7746, beta 0.7612. No single gained more than +0.001, so the combined stack was not run.

**Held-out, window=all, difference vs warm(hebbian-robust)**, in the order fixed / random / no-traps / static control:
- **(a) Alpha** (oscillating exploration): −0.0051 / −0.0006 / −0.0037 / −0.0042. None of the 40 tuned configs beat plain warm.
  - It is no better than a mean-matched constant or a phase-randomised control. Differences vs those controls are −0.006 to +0.001, mostly with CIs spanning 0. Against the mean-matched constant it is significantly worse on fixed (−0.0040) and no-traps (−0.0056).
  - So there is no sign the oscillation structure helps.
- **(b) Gamma**
  - Gate: +0.0003 / +0.0019 / +0.0019 / +0.0017, all non-significant. It only benches dead agents, and a random-burst version is identical to within 0.0001.
  - Batch consolidation: −0.0036 / +0.0081 [+0.0020, +0.0141] / +0.0009 / +0.0024. The random-world gain has a raw CI above 0 but Holm p=1, and it is negative on fixed.
  - Random-time batching is as good or better than periodic batching, so it is not an oscillation effect.
- **(c) Theta-gamma replay** (k=2/4/8): k=2 is −0.0011 / +0.0036 / +0.0016 / +0.0006, all non-significant. k=4 and k=8 are worse on fixed and no-traps (k=4 −0.0093 on fixed; its mean-matched eta control is better by about 0.009).
  - Replay is no better than eta-matched no-replay or random-time replay.
- **(d) Beta status-quo:** −0.0188 / −0.0081 / −0.0133 / −0.0130. Holm-significant losses on fixed (also in its failure window) and on the static control; on no-traps the significant loss is against keyword.
  - The never-release and matched-random-release controls are no better. Tuned burst rate was 0.367.

**Other observations**
- In no-traps, keyword (0.793) is the best fair baseline and everything here loses to it. None of the oscillation wrappers beats keyword there.
- The static control behaves as expected: nothing helps, and alpha and beta cost accuracy.
- Verdict I believe: reject all four. The warm-started robust Hebbian router is already near its ceiling in these worlds, and extra exploration or stickiness only costs accuracy.
- `cargo test --release --lib` currently has one failing test, `cognition::tests::hier_isolates_domains`. That file belongs to another team; my tests pass (146 passed, 1 failed overall).

No packages were installed and no security findings.
